correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs all three variants from their defining structural characterizations. Total general position is controlled by the two degree-one simplicial vertices. Outer general position is controlled by an exact classification of mutually maximally distant pairs: precisely the cross nonedges at distance three. Dual general position is controlled by convex complements; explicit length-two geodesics through any non-extreme selected vertex and a separate adjacent-pair argument eliminate all competitors. A direct-definition exhaustive checker independently verifies all maximum families for orders four through seven.

value.rationale: The three variants were introduced to separate distinct shortest-path visibility requirements, and half graphs are a canonical chain-graph family already used in later general-position research. The result shows an instructive scalar collapse with a sharp extremal-set divergence: total and dual optima are uniquely the two leaves, while outer optima comprise every diametral cross nonedge. The exact strong-resolving-graph description and complete maximum-set counts are reusable structural information.
